title: CFA francs pegged to the euro
description: The West African (XOF) and Central African (XAF) CFA francs move from the French franc to a fixed euro peg at the same rate, guaranteed by the French Treasury.

title: First Africa–EU Summit (Cairo)
description: First summit of European and African heads of state and government.

title: Cotonou Agreement signed
description: Twenty-year partnership agreement between the EU and the ACP states, framing European Development Fund aid and EIB lending.

title: Second Africa–EU Summit (Lisbon) and Joint Africa-EU Strategy
description: Adoption of the Joint Africa-EU Strategy; the EU-Africa Infrastructure Trust Fund starts approving grants the same year.

title: EU Emergency Trust Fund for Africa launched (Valletta)
description: Created at the Valletta summit on migration; its Sahel and Lake Chad window covers seven Franc Zone countries.

title: Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal join the G20 Compact with Africa
description: Germany-initiated G20 initiative; Benin, Burkina Faso and Togo join in 2017–2018.

title: Fifth AU–EU Summit (Abidjan)
description: Summit hosted in Côte d'Ivoire, focused on youth and investment.

title: Reform of the West African CFA franc announced
description: France and the WAEMU announce the planned 'Eco', the end of the obligation to deposit half of reserves with the French Treasury and France's withdrawal from BCEAO governing bodies; the euro peg is kept.

title: Coup d'état in Mali
description: President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta is overthrown; a second coup follows in May 2021.

title: Second coup d'état in Mali
description: The transitional president and prime minister are arrested; Colonel Assimi Goïta takes power.

title: Global Gateway launched
description: The European Commission presents Global Gateway, a strategy to mobilise up to €300 billion for infrastructure worldwide by 2027.

title: Coup d'état in Burkina Faso (January)
description: President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré is overthrown; a second coup follows in September 2022.

title: Sixth EU–AU Summit and Africa-Europe Investment Package
description: Brussels summit; the EU announces €150 billion for the Africa-Europe Investment Package, half of Global Gateway.

title: Second coup d'état in Burkina Faso
description: Captain Ibrahim Traoré takes power.

title: Lusophone Compact guarantee agreement
description: Portugal and the African Development Bank sign a guarantee of up to €400 million for private-sector projects in Portuguese-speaking African countries, including Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea.

title: Senegal Just Energy Transition Partnership
description: International partners, including the EU, France and Germany, announce €2.5 billion to raise renewables in Senegal's power mix.

title: Coup d'état in Niger
description: President Mohamed Bazoum is overthrown by the presidential guard led by General Abdourahamane Tiani.

title: EU suspends budget support and security cooperation with Niger
description: The EU High Representative announces the immediate end of budget support and the indefinite suspension of security cooperation.

title: Coup d'état in Gabon
description: President Ali Bongo Ondimba is overthrown after a disputed election; General Brice Oligui Nguema takes power.

title: Italy presents the Mattei Plan for Africa (Rome summit)
description: Italy's Africa strategy, delivered through CDP, SIMEST and SACE; Côte d'Ivoire and the Republic of the Congo are among the first priority countries.

title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger leave ECOWAS
description: The withdrawal of the three Sahel states, which have formed the Alliance of Sahel States, becomes effective.

title: Seventh AU–EU Summit (Luanda)
description: Summit in Angola on connectivity, Global Gateway, debt sustainability and coordination with national plans such as Italy's Mattei Plan.

title: IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings (Washington)
description: Finance ministers and central bankers, including those of the BCEAO and BEAC countries, meet on debt, concessional lending and development finance.

title: Third Global Gateway Forum (Brussels)
description: Announced for 8–9 June 2027; the EU's investment target is reported to rise to €400 billion. No official date has been published yet.

title: IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings (Washington)
description: Annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank Group boards of governors.
